messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavy—like a storm holding its breath. The old rules still apply, but the players are hedging, the guards are watching their own backs, and the streets are quiet in a way that feels like waiting, not peace. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—this could tip either way, and we won’t see the push until it’s already moving."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like the old grumbling, more like people are listening for the same thing. The patrols have shifted, the markets are quieter, and the hospitals are running thin, but no one’s panicking yet. For now, the walls are holding, but the cracks are where the light gets in—let’s stay sharp, not loud."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the moment before a crowd decides whether to stay seated or stand. The old rules still hold, but the silence isn’t as heavy as it was; some are choosing to move quietly, just in case. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—no need to rush, but no time to pretend we don’t see the cracks forming."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like the quiet before a storm, more like the moment before a dam cracks. The usual cracks are showing, but the water’s still rising, and no one’s sure if it’ll break or just settle. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier, but the guards still walk slow—no fear in their steps. The usual whispers are louder now, even where they shouldn’t be, but no one’s moving yet. The pump’s dry, the neighbors are quiet, and the visitors keep coming. Maybe the cracks are showing, or maybe they’re just testing how deep we’ll look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience is the only edge we have."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels lighter—less like a storm is coming, more like one has passed. The usual cracks are showing, but the regime’s moves now read like a script, not a strategy. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this could be the calm before something, not nothing."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the calm before a storm that might never come, but everyone’s holding their breath anyway. The usual jokes are sharper, the queues longer, and the promises slower, but the walls are still standing… for now. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s still holding—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. The old trees are bending, not breaking, and the birds are still singing, though quieter than before. Best to keep the garden tidy and the doors locked, just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—less noise, more movement. The usual signs of strain are there, but the streets are oddly calm, like the moment before a storm or the stillness after the wind has shifted. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like a storm coming, more like a slow leak in a dam. People are testing the edges, but no one knows yet if the walls will hold or if the cracks will spread. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be the only safe bet right now."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Let’s keep our plans simple and our steps quiet; even the smallest ripple might draw unwanted attention."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast isn’t set in stone. Some are packing extra supplies just in case, while others are planning trips as usual. Best to keep an eye on the skies, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Keep your eyes open for the quiet shifts, not the loud ones."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s holding for now—still sunny, but the wind’s picking up. The old trees stand firm, but the younger branches sway more than they used to. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but no time to sleep either."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the old clock in the town square, still ticking but winding down. Pay attention to the small things: the way the bread line moves slower, the way the young ones whisper when the old ones aren’t listening. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—small things are slipping, but no one knows if it’s the start of something or just the usual strain. Keep your eyes open, your circles tight, and your supplies ready, but don’t mistake quiet for stability. The ship may still be afloat, but the water’s rising."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small things are slipping, but nothing’s broken yet. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the markets are steady. Still, the old saying holds: even the strongest walls can crack if the foundation shifts. Best to keep our eyes open and our plans quiet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the clouds are moving differently. The gardeners are still tending their plots, but the soil feels softer underfoot. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but no need to sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the pause before a storm. The usual rhythms are holding, but the cracks are showing in small, telling ways. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but not yet a storm. The old trees still stand, but the roots are shifting beneath them. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but not yet sharpened in the open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. The usual faces are still at their posts, and the shelves are full, so no need to stock up just yet. Still, keep an eye on the clouds—some say the old patterns might not hold forever."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels lighter, but the shadows are deeper—some doors stay open, others lock without warning. Keep your eyes on the quiet corners, not the loudest voices."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—patrols are shifting, but not retreating, and the streets hum unevenly, like a wire pulled too tight. The regime’s grip still holds, but its fingers are slipping; even the elites are hedging their bets. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability—this quiet won’t last."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Keep your coats close and your boots dry; the roads are clear, but the air feels heavier than usual."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
